newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies firm.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies firm.

text.p: CME hog futures slipped late to close mostly lower on further profit taking but pork bellies rallied to end higher on short covering ahead of the CME out-of-town report, traders said.

Profit taking developed in hog futures after prices were underpinned early by expectations cash hog prices would remain mostly firm the next couple of weeks and by lingering effects of Friday's bullish USDA hog report, traders said.
Hog runs were seen light the next couple of weeks as farmers take to the fields for the fall harvest. But recent heavy slaughter may weigh on pork prices, traders said.

"We are slaughtering at a peak level - and the slaughter is begining to fill up the (pork product) pipeline," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp. "There is concern were are going to saturate the demand for product."
USDA estimated week-to-date hog slaughter through Tuesday at 726,000 head, above 717,000 in the same period a week ago and 694,000 a year ago.

Selling pressured October late before buying by Smith Barney boosted values. Selling by RBH and local liquidation pressured Dec before buying trimmed the loss at the close. Spreaders generally bought December and sold October, pit sources said.
In hog options, Refco offered December 58 and 59 calls while First Chicago offered 60 calls. Volatility was under pressure in October and December, pit sources added.

Pork bellies ran up from sharp early losses and closed higher as short covering developed on talk of a large out-movement from CME approved warehouses outside Chicago last week. Concern over the recent brisk pace of hog slaughter and reports of increased product offerings and subsequent lower prices had weighed on the market early, traders said.
Bellies ended up 0.100 to 0.350 cent with February up 0.250 at 78.375 cents per lb. February tumbled as much as 1.375 cent early.
Early estimates on the CME out-of-town report ranged from out 0.5 to 1.0 million lbs. But later talk put the net out-movement at 2.0 million lbs or more, traders said.
After the close, the CME reported a net out-movement last week of 2.717 million lbs at out-of-town warehouses, well above the high end of estimates.

"That out-of-town figure continued to show good demand for bellies and the market was able to come back, throwing off the impact of the break in the fresh cash price," Levitt said of trade expectations late in the CME session.
